easy.def: A hot drink made with leaves.
examples: Grandma drinks tea.
Mom made a cup of tea.
Tea is hot.

more.def: A drink made by pouring hot water over dried leaves.
examples: My grandmother has a cup of tea every afternoon.
She added honey to her tea.
Tea is grown on hillside farms.
Mom teaches me to cook.
She taught us a song.
He teaches art.

more.def: To show someone how to do something or give lessons in a subject.
examples: My grandfather taught me how to play chess.
She teaches music at the elementary school.
Parents teach their children to share.

easy.def: A person who helps you learn at school.
examples: My teacher reads to us.
The teacher is kind.
A teacher helps us.

more.def: A person whose job is to teach students.
examples: The teacher handed out the spelling tests.
My piano teacher plays beautiful songs.
Our science teacher brought in a snake.

easy.def: A group that works or plays together.
examples: Our team won the game.
I am on a soccer team.
The team shared the trophy.

more.def: A group of people who play a sport or work together toward the same goal.
examples: Our soccer team practices twice a week.
A team of scientists studied the volcano for years.
The two teams shook hands after the game.
Do not tear the paper.
I tore my shirt.
She tears the bread.

more.def: To pull something apart or into pieces.
examples: Please do not tear the pages of the book.
He tore a hole in his jeans on the fence.
She tore the bread into small pieces.

easy.def: A drop of water from your eye.
examples: A tear ran down her cheek.
I wiped a tear from my eye.
The onion brought a tear.

more.def: A drop of salty water that comes from your eye when you cry.
examples: A single tear rolled down his cheek.
She wiped a tear from her eye.
Tears of joy filled his eyes.
There is a tear in my shirt.
Tape the tear in the page.
The tear is small.

more.def: A hole or split made by pulling something apart.
examples: There is a long tear in my backpack.
She sewed up a tear in her sleeve.
A tear in the page made it hard to read.

easy.def: A tool that makes far away things look big.
examples: I saw the moon with a telescope.
The telescope is on a stand.
He looked at a ship with a telescope.

more.def: A tool you look through that makes distant things, like stars, appear larger and closer.
examples: Through the telescope, we could see the rings of Saturn.
The sailor spotted land through his telescope.
A huge telescope on the mountain studies distant stars.
Tell me a story.
She told me her name.
I will tell Mom.

more.def: To give someone information, a story, or an order by speaking.
examples: Please tell the class what you learned on your trip.
The guide told us not to touch the old paintings.
My grandfather tells funny stories about his boat.

easy.def: How hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature is cold today.
What is the temperature outside?
The nurse took my temperature.

more.def: A measure of how hot or cold something is.
examples: The temperature dropped below freezing, and the pond turned to ice.
Bake the cake at a low temperature.
The temperature of the ocean is rising.
I have ten fingers.
Count to ten.
Ten kids are in line.

more.def: The number 10, which is one more than nine.
examples: A dime is worth ten cents.
She counted by tens up to a hundred.
The cookies bake for ten minutes.
I had a terrible dream.
The milk smells terrible.
I have a terrible cold.
A terrible storm knocked out the power for two days.
The roads were in terrible shape after the flood.
He felt terrible about forgetting her birthday.

easy.def: Questions that show what you know.
examples: We have a spelling test.
I got every answer right on the test.
The math test was easy.

more.def: A set of questions or tasks that shows how much you know or can do.
examples: I studied hard for my science test.
The vision test at school was easy.
Each student took a spelling test on Friday.

easy.def: To try something to see how it works.
examples: We test the boat in the tub.
She tested the water with her toe.
Dad tests the smoke alarm.

more.def: To try something out to find out how well it works or what it is.
examples: Scientists tested the new robot in the lab.
She tested the water with her toe before jumping in.
We tested which paper towel soaks up the most water.
